entities.name: Hellenistic Period
entities.label: Timeframe
entities.summary: The era (323-31 BCE) from Alexander the Great's death to Rome's annexation of Egypt, during which Greek culture spread across the Near East, Central Asia, and North Africa. Hellenistic kingdoms blended Greek and local traditions, producing advances in science (Euclid, Archimedes), philosophy (Stoicism, Epicureanism), and art that profoundly influenced Roman and later Western culture.
